_note: The reusable prompt system. Each entry in 'formats' is a DISTINCT composition with its own creative direction, not one template resized - that is what separates a strong asset from a weak one. The model generates the whole poster, lettering included, so the type sits in the paper world and carries its grain. Add a theme to get a seasonal set; nothing else needs editing.
base: Flat graphic cut-paper collage, designed as a poster, NOT a photograph. Every element is cut or torn from textured paper and laid flat: clean geometric planes, hard fold lines shown as straight edges between two tones, deliberately torn edges with a soft deckled fibre lip, visible paper grain inside every shape, crisp cut edges. Screen-printed risograph feel with limited flat inks. The composition is DENSE and LAYERED, with real depth from overlapping planes and a soft contact shadow where one sheet sits on another - rich and balanced, never sparse, never a large empty field.
palette_rule: Strictly three flat inks: warm off-white paper as the ground, deep warm near-black, and exactly one saturated warm amber as the single accent, used boldly on large shapes. No other hue anywhere. No blue, no green, no pink, no teal, no pastel yellow.
negative: NOT a photograph: no photographic realism, no depth of field, no studio lighting, no cast shadows, no 3D rendering, no origami cranes or animals, no desk scene, no props, no plants, no leaves, no flowers, no hands, no people. Apart from those two lines of type, add no other words, no numbers, no labels, no signature, no watermark, no logo. Do not misspell anything. No gradients, no vignette, no sepia.

banner.composition: A torn vertical edge splits the frame: calm paper on the left carrying the lettering, and on the right a dense amber field with the cup drawn as a white cut-paper outline, a small cut-paper note bearing the cup mark, a printed coffee ring, scattered beans and layered kraft planes receding into a dark plane at the corner. 2:1 and 1.9:1 crops are taken from the vertical centre, so keep the very top and bottom edges quieter than the middle.

square.composition: A centred poster: the cup is the hero, large, drawn as a white cut-paper outline on a bold amber plane filling the lower two thirds, with layered kraft and dark planes radiating out behind it and a printed ring overlapping the lower edge. The stacked two-line name sits in the upper third on clean paper. Balanced, iconic, dense. Used at 1:1 with no crop.

portrait.composition: A tall stack: the stacked two-line name on paper at the top, a wide torn amber band across the middle carrying the cup as a large white cut-paper outline, and beneath it layered kraft and dark planes with a printed ring and a small note overlapping them. The eye travels straight down, dense all the way to the bottom edge. A 9:16 crop trims the sides, so keep the lettering and the focal elements inside the central three quarters of the width.

ultrawide.composition: A frieze: a continuous horizontal rhythm of cut-paper elements marching across the strip - the lettering at the left, then a torn amber plane, the cup as a white outline, a printed ring, a small note, a trio of beans, and a dark plane closing the right end. Each element overlaps its neighbour so the strip reads as one dense band with no gaps. A 5.9:1 crop is taken from a shallow strip at the exact vertical centre, so EVERYTHING must sit inside the middle quarter of the height, lettering included and scaled down to fit it.

wide3.composition: A long panoramic counter: layered paper planes running the FULL width in an unbroken horizontal rhythm, a torn amber sweep crossing behind, the cup as a large white cut-paper outline just right of centre, a printed ring and scattered beans to its right, a dark angular plane anchoring the far right. The lettering sits on the left, over paper, with the layers continuing behind it. A 3:1 crop is taken from the middle half of the height, so every part of that centre band must be occupied - no empty stretches anywhere along it.

xheader.composition: Bold and graphic, the opposite of a panorama: a huge amber field occupies the right two thirds as a single confident plane, the cup reversed out of it as a clean white cut-paper outline at generous scale, a dark angular plane cutting in from the lower left, and a small printed ring overlapping the join. The lettering sits on the remaining paper at the left. Few elements, large, high contrast. A 3:1 crop is taken from the middle half of the height.

emailheader.composition: Editorial and typographic: mostly warm paper, with ONE strong amber torn diagonal running from the lower left to the upper right behind the type, a small stack of cut-paper notes with the cup mark on the top one, and a printed ring sitting half on the paper and half on the amber. The lettering is the hero and sits large across the left two thirds. Quiet and confident, but still layered. A 3:1 crop is taken from the middle half of the height.

themes.halloween: One cut-paper crescent and one angular bat silhouette sit among the planes; the accent deepens toward burnt orange. Still three flat inks.
themes.christmas: One folded paper star and one narrow cut snowflake sit among the planes; the accent warms toward gold. Still three flat inks.
themes.easter: One cut-paper egg shape and one torn arc sit among the planes. Still three flat inks.
themes.wald: A row of angular cut-paper pine silhouettes runs along the lower edge. Still three flat inks.

lettering: THIS IS A TYPOGRAPHIC POSTER. The single word "Kaffeelisten" is the main subject, large and clearly readable in the calm area. Spell it EXACTLY K-a-f-f-e-e-l-i-s-t-e-n as one unbroken word with no space and no hyphen. SET IT IN TWO COLOURS WITHIN THE ONE WORD: the first six letters "Kaffee" in the deep warm near-black ink, and the last six letters "listen" in the saturated warm amber. The colour change happens mid-word with no gap. A clean modern geometric sans-serif, heavy weight, tight letter-spacing, printed flat on the paper so it carries the paper's grain. Directly beneath it, much smaller and lighter in near-black, the line "Die Kaffeeliste - ohne Papier." Letterforms crisp, even and correctly formed.
lettering_stacked: THIS IS A TYPOGRAPHIC POSTER. The name is set on TWO LINES, stacked and left-aligned, reading "Kaffee" on the first line and "listen" on the second line - together they spell the single word Kaffeelisten. "Kaffee" is in the deep warm near-black ink and "listen" directly beneath it is in the saturated warm amber. Tight line spacing so the two lines read as one block. A clean modern geometric sans-serif, heavy weight, tight letter-spacing, printed flat on the paper so it carries the paper's grain. Beneath the block, much smaller and lighter in near-black, the line "Die Kaffeeliste - ohne Papier." Letterforms crisp, even and correctly formed. Spell both words exactly: K-a-f-f-e-e and l-i-s-t-e-n.
